## Open

### F-227 — The flow list did not contain the execution its own call had just served

> _2026-09-21 · realm/blong-gateway · open_

`realm/blong-gateway`'s diagram spec flaked in CI and locally on `blong.flow.find`: the flow page's
table still showed "Nothing observed yet" seven seconds after the spec had served
`gateway.bundle.find` — the very execution it then looked for. Measured with a probe inside the
spec: `executionsInDom: 0`, `emptyMessages: 1`, `errorText: null`, so the read had not failed — it
was an answer that simply did not contain the row. The page reads once (`useRealmRead` re-reads only
when its parameters change) and nothing re-reads, so a second answer has to be asked for; a reload
keeps the session and the permissions (`token/restore`), which is how the spec asks for one. Two
wrong diagnoses were ruled out with the same probe: the filter is not the problem (once the answer
is in the table the kind's row appears), and the first row being another spec's execution was the
older failure (`gateway.subscription.find`), not this one.

The spec now retries producing-and-reading as a pair (`expect(...).toPass`) — five clean suite runs
where it had been two in three flaking.

Still open, and the real defect: the service's list lags the call that produced the entry, or the
read is served from a snapshot, so a caller cannot rely on "I called it, therefore it is listed".
Worth looking at when the ledger publishes and how `blong.flow.find` assembles its answer, and at
whether a page that lists executions should re-read when it is shown rather than only when it is
first opened.
